items.stem: On enlistment morning the web servers handle every request, but seat reservations are slow. The university doubles the number of web servers. What happens to the speed of reservations?

options.text: Very little changes, because the single primary database is the limit.
options.feedback: Every reservation is a change to the database, and one primary has to handle them in order. More web servers only send it more requests.
The web servers were already coping, and reservations wait for the database.

options.text: Reservations become slower, because the servers fight each other.
options.feedback: More web servers do not slow the system down. They do not change the database limit.

items.stem: Which change reduces the peak load on the database without buying any hardware?

options.text: Give each year level its own enlistment time slot.
options.feedback: Spreading the arrivals over time lowers the peak rate, and the system needs no extra machines.
This adds capacity to the web tier, which was not the limit.

options.text: Move the web servers to the cloud with autoscaling.
options.feedback: Autoscaling also fixes the web tier only. The database primary stays the same.

items.stem: Before you try it: 4,000 students enlist in a 10-minute window, with no staggering and no separation of browsing from reserving. In the on-premise case with 7 web servers, which tier is overloaded?

options.feedback: The peak is about 600 requests per second, which is under the web tier maximum of 700.
The web tier copes with 600 requests per second, but all 600 operations per second reach a primary database that handles 400.
The peak is under the web tier maximum of 700 requests per second. Only the database is over its maximum.

items.try: Leave both switches off, read the verdict, then select the Now: cloud case.

items.stem: A student suggests sending seat reservations to read-only replicas of the database to spread the load. Why does this not work?

options.text: A reservation changes data, so one primary must decide who gets the last seat.
options.feedback: Replicas only answer reads. If two copies each accepted a reservation, both students could get the same seat.

options.text: Replicas are too slow to handle reservation requests during the enlistment peak.
options.feedback: Speed is not the issue. Replicas cannot accept changes.

options.text: Reservations can be cached at the web tier, so replicas are not needed.
options.feedback: A cached answer can be out of date. A reservation needs the current seat count.
